paragraphs.source_en: I decided to leave sea-bathing for the future, but to take up exercise at once. In this twentieth century, not exercising makes one sound rather like a pauper, and the reputation is not pleasant. When I do not exercise, it is not that I do not wish to; it is that I cannot: I am judged to have no time for exercise, no leisure allotted to it. Formerly, people who liked exercise were laughed at as errand-running menials in samurai households; nowadays, those who do not exercise are regarded as inferior people. The world's estimation changes constantly with time and circumstance, just like my humble eyeballs. My eyeballs merely grow larger and smaller, but human judgments can turn completely upside down. Of course, there is no harm in turning upside down. Everything has two faces; everything has two ends. The human gift for adaptability lies precisely in making black and white, right and wrong, arise in one and the same thing. Turn fangcun around and it becomes cunfang; therein lies the charm of mankind. Look at Amanohashidate from between one's legs, and it takes on quite another savor. If Shakespeare were always the immutable Shakespeare of all ages, he would be dreadfully dull; unless someone now and then looks at Hamlet from between his legs and says, My dear fellow, this is no good, then the literary world would never make progress. Therefore there is nothing at all strange in the former detractors of exercise suddenly becoming fond of it, or even in women walking about the streets carrying rackets. So long as they do not laugh at a cat's taking part in exercise as an act of presumption, all is well. Wait a moment. Some may perhaps wonder what kind of exercise I mean to undertake, so I should like to offer a brief explanation.

units.source_en: I decided to leave sea-bathing for the future, but to take up exercise at once.
units.source_zh: 海水浴待将来再说，但我却下决心去搞一搞运动。

units.source_en: In this twentieth century, not exercising makes one sound rather like a pauper, and the reputation is not pleasant.
units.source_zh: 在二十世纪的今天，不进行运动就像个贫民，名声不太好听。

units.source_en: When I do not exercise, it is not that I do not wish to; it is that I cannot: I am judged to have no time for exercise, no leisure allotted to it.
units.source_zh: 我不运动，并不是不想运动，而是不能运动，是我没有运动的时间，被注定无运动的余暇。

units.source_en: Formerly, people who liked exercise were laughed at as errand-running menials in samurai households; nowadays, those who do not exercise are regarded as inferior people.
units.source_zh: 过去，喜好运动的人被讥笑为武士家去干跑腿这一行当的奴仆，如今，不运动的人则被看作是下等人。

units.source_en: The world's estimation changes constantly with time and circumstance, just like my humble eyeballs.
units.source_zh: 世人的评价，根据时间和情况在不断变换，就像在下的眼珠一样。

units.source_en: My eyeballs merely grow larger and smaller, but human judgments can turn completely upside down.

ja.t: きくなったりするばかりだが、

units.source_zh: 我的眼珠只不过是变大变小而已，但人的品评却会整个颠倒过来。

units.source_en: Of course, there is no harm in turning upside down.
units.source_zh: 颠倒过来当然不要紧。

units.source_en: Everything has two faces; everything has two ends.
units.source_zh: 事物总有两面，总有两端。

units.source_en: The human gift for adaptability lies precisely in making black and white, right and wrong, arise in one and the same thing.
units.source_zh: 在同一事物上使其产生出黑白是非的变化，这点正是人的圆滑融通之处。

units.source_en: Turn fangcun around and it becomes cunfang; therein lies the charm of mankind.
units.source_zh: 将“方寸”颠倒过来就成了“寸方”，这正是人的可爱之点。

units.source_en: Look at Amanohashidate from between one's legs, and it takes on quite another savor.
units.source_zh: 从两股间去看“天之桥立”，就会又别有一番情趣。

units.source_en: If Shakespeare were always the immutable Shakespeare of all ages, he would be dreadfully dull; unless someone now and then looks at Hamlet from between his legs and says, My dear fellow, this is no good,

ja.t: セクスピヤではつまらない。

units.source_zh: 莎士比亚如果总是千古不易的莎士比亚，也就无味得很，如果没有人偶尔从两股间去看一看《哈姆雷特》，说：“老兄，这没什么了不起。”

units.source_en: then the literary world would never make progress.
units.source_zh: 那么文艺界也就不会发展。

units.source_en: Therefore there is nothing at all strange in the former detractors of exercise suddenly becoming fond of it, or even in women walking about the streets carrying rackets.
units.source_zh: 所以过去说运动坏话的一伙人，现在忽然爱好起运动来，甚至连妇女都拿着球拍在街上走来走去，这些都毫不足怪。

units.source_en: So long as they do not laugh at a cat's taking part in exercise as an act of presumption, all is well.

ja.t: いさえしなければよい。

units.source_zh: 只要不把猫儿参加运动也讥笑为狂妄之举就可以了。

units.source_en: Wait a moment.
units.source_zh: 且慢！

units.source_en: Some may perhaps wonder what kind of exercise I mean to undertake, so I should like to offer a brief explanation.
units.source_zh: 也许有人会产生疑问，不知道我要搞的是哪种运动，为此我想略加说明。

paragraphs.source_zh: 海水浴待将来再说，但我却下决心去搞一搞运动。在二十世纪的今天，不进行运动就像个贫民，名声不太好听。我不运动，并不是不想运动，而是不能运动，是我没有运动的时间，被注定无运动的余暇。过去，喜好运动的人被讥笑为武士家去干跑腿这一行当的奴仆，如今，不运动的人则被看作是下等人。世人的评价，根据时间和情况在不断变换，就像在下的眼珠一样。我的眼珠只不过是变大变小而已，但人的品评却会整个颠倒过来。颠倒过来当然不要紧。事物总有两面，总有两端。在同一事物上使其产生出黑白是非的变化，这点正是人的圆滑融通之处。将“方寸”颠倒过来就成了“寸方”，这正是人的可爱之点。从两股间去看“天之桥立”，就会又别有一番情趣。莎士比亚如果总是千古不易的莎士比亚，也就无味得很，如果没有人偶尔从两股间去看一看《哈姆雷特》，说：“老兄，这没什么了不起。”那么文艺界也就不会发展。所以过去说运动坏话的一伙人，现在忽然爱好起运动来，甚至连妇女都拿着球拍在街上走来走去，这些都毫不足怪。只要不把猫儿参加运动也讥笑为狂妄之举就可以了。且慢！也许有人会产生疑问，不知道我要搞的是哪种运动，为此我想略加说明。

paragraphs.source_en: As you know, we cats unfortunately cannot hold implements, so we are at a loss as to how to handle bats or balls; besides, even if we could use them, we have no money to buy them. For these two reasons, the exercise I chose had to belong to the kind that costs nothing and has nothing to do with apparatus. Given that, some may suppose I might stroll about at leisure, or dash off with a slice of tuna in my mouth. But merely setting my four legs in mechanical motion and roaming over the earth under the influence of gravity is far too simple and dull. Though it bears the name exercise, if it merely moves about in the literal sense, as my master often does, I consider it a defilement of the sacred meaning of exercise. Of course, ordinary exercise too may be performed under a certain stimulus. Games such as a tuna-snatching race or hunting for salmon are quite entertaining. But in such cases the object is indispensable; remove the stimulus of the object and they become flat and tasteless. If these prize-like stimulants are excluded, then I should like to try an exercise with some skill in it. So I thought up various methods. Exercises such as jumping from the kitchen awning onto the roof, the art of standing on all four legs upon the plum-blossom-shaped tiles along the ridge, or running across the clothes pole; this last, after all, can scarcely be expected to succeed, because the bamboo pole is so slippery that one's claws cannot grip it. There is also suddenly springing onto a child from behind; this is an exercise of considerable interest, but if done often it brings terrible misfortune, so I try it at most three times a month. Putting a paper bag over my head: this brings only suffering and is a game of little interest; besides, unless some human cooperates with me, it cannot be carried out, so that will not do either. Then there is scratching the covers of books with my claws; once my master discovers this exercise, not only is there a great likelihood of being beaten, but it trains only the dexterity of the claws and not the muscles of the whole body. All of the above belong to the contents of old-style exercise. Among the new-style exercises there are some that are extremely interesting; first comes mantis hunting. Mantis hunting is not such great exercise as mouse hunting, but neither does it involve very great danger. From midsummer into early autumn, this game is of the very first rank. As for the method of catching one, I first go out into the garden and look for a mantis; when the season is right, finding one or two is no trouble at all. Then I run like a gust of wind to the mantis's side. At that moment, seeing an enemy approach, the mantis at once assumes a posture and raises its two sickle-like forelegs high. The mantis too is a creature of considerable courage; before it has learned its opponent's strength, it always wants to have a bout, which is most amusing. When I flick my right forepaw toward its raised forelegs, its very soft, lifted head immediately droops weakly to one side; its expression then is wonderfully amusing, a look of complete bewilderment.

units.source_en: As you know, we cats unfortunately cannot hold implements, so we are at a loss as to how to handle bats or balls; besides, even if we could use them, we have no money to buy them.

ja.t: ん。だからボールもバットも

units.source_zh: 如尊驾所知，我们猫儿不幸的是拿不了道具的，所以对于垒球棒啦、球啦，都不知道如何使用，加上即使会用，我们也没有钱去买。

units.source_en: For these two reasons, the exercise I chose had to belong to the kind that costs nothing and has nothing to do with apparatus.
units.source_zh: 由于这两个原因，所以我选择的运动，必须是属于那种既不需要花费，也与运动器械无关的。

units.source_en: Given that, some may suppose I might stroll about at leisure, or dash off with a slice of tuna in my mouth.
units.source_zh: 既然是这样，也许有人会认为我可以慢条斯理地走走路或者叼着一片金枪鱼飞跑。

units.source_en: But merely setting my four legs in mechanical motion and roaming over the earth under the influence of gravity is far too simple and dull.
units.source_zh: 但是只让我的四条腿做力学运动，利用地球引力的作用在大地上闯来闯去，未免过于简单乏味。

units.source_en: Though it bears the name exercise, if it merely moves about in the literal sense, as my master often does, I consider it a defilement of the sacred meaning of exercise.
units.source_zh: 尽管名称叫运动，但它像主人经常做的那样，只是在字面上运动来运动去，我认为这是玷污运动的神圣意义。

units.source_en: Of course, ordinary exercise too may be performed under a certain stimulus.
units.source_zh: 当然，就是一般的运动，如果在某种刺激之下，也不一定不可以做。

units.source_en: Games such as a tuna-snatching race or hunting for salmon are quite entertaining.
units.source_zh: 像“抢金枪鱼赛跑”、“寻找大马哈鱼”这类玩意儿，也是蛮有意思的。

units.source_en: But in such cases the object is indispensable; remove the stimulus of the object and they become flat and tasteless.

ja.t: なものになってしまう。

units.source_zh: 不过，这种场合缺不了对象，如果去掉对象的刺激，就变得索然寡味了。

units.source_en: If these prize-like stimulants are excluded, then I should like to try an exercise with some skill in it.
units.source_zh: 假如排除这些奖赏性的刺激物，那么我倒是想搞点带技巧性的运动。

units.source_en: So I thought up various methods.
units.source_zh: 于是，我想出了各种方法。

units.source_en: Exercises such as jumping from the kitchen awning onto the roof, the art of standing on all four legs upon the plum-blossom-shaped tiles along the ridge, or running across the clothes pole; this last, after all, can scarcely be expected to succeed, because the bamboo pole is so slippery that one's claws cannot grip it.
units.source_zh: 像从厨房的遮阳板跳到屋顶上去的运动，在屋脊的梅花形屋瓦上用四条腿站立的技巧，从晾衣竿上跑过去——这毕竟是难以指望成功的，因为竹竿滑溜溜的无法下爪子。

units.source_en: There is also suddenly springing onto a child from behind; this is an exercise of considerable interest, but if done often it brings terrible misfortune, so I try it at most three times a month.
units.source_zh: 还有从背后突然蹦到小孩身上——这虽是饶有兴味的运动，但经常搞就会大触霉头，所以至多每个月搞上三次。

units.source_en: Putting a paper bag over my head: this brings only suffering and is a game of little interest; besides, unless some human cooperates with me, it cannot be carried out, so that will not do either.

ja.t: しいばかりではなはだ

units.source_zh: 往头上套纸袋——这只能感到痛苦，是种兴趣不大的玩法，而且这种运动假如没有人和我合作，也无法进行，所以也不行。

units.source_en: Then there is scratching the covers of books with my claws; once my master discovers this exercise, not only is there a great likelihood of being beaten, but it trains only the dexterity of the claws and not the muscles of the whole body.
units.source_zh: 还有用我的爪子扒搔书的封皮，——这个运动一旦被主人发觉，不仅大有挨揍的可能，而且只锻炼了爪子的灵巧，不能锻炼浑身的肌肉。

units.source_en: All of the above belong to the contents of old-style exercise.
units.source_zh: 以上这些，都是旧式运动的内容。

units.source_en: Among the new-style exercises there are some that are extremely interesting; first comes mantis hunting.
units.source_zh: 在新式运动中，有些是非常有趣的，首先是捕螳螂。

units.source_en: Mantis hunting is not such great exercise as mouse hunting, but neither does it involve very great danger.
units.source_zh: 捕螳螂虽不是捕老鼠那样的大运动，但它也不会有很大的危险。

units.source_en: From midsummer into early autumn, this game is of the very first rank.
units.source_zh: 从仲夏到初秋这段期间，这种游戏是最属上乘的。

units.source_en: As for the method of catching one, I first go out into the garden and look for a mantis; when the season is right, finding one or two is no trouble at all.
units.source_zh: 至于说到捕捉的方法，我先到院中去寻出一只螳螂来，如果气候好，找出一两只是毫不费力的。

units.source_en: Then I run like a gust of wind to the mantis's side.
units.source_zh: 然后，我就一阵风似的跑到螳螂身旁。

units.source_en: At that moment, seeing an enemy approach, the mantis at once assumes a posture and raises its two sickle-like forelegs high.
units.source_zh: 这时螳螂一见来敌，立刻摆好架势，高高举起它那两个镰刀状的前脚。

units.source_en: The mantis too is a creature of considerable courage; before it has learned its opponent's strength, it always wants to have a bout, which is most amusing.

ja.t: するつもりでいるから

units.source_zh: 螳螂也是胆量很大的家伙，在没有领教对手的力量之前，总想较量一番，真是有意思极啦。

units.source_en: When I flick my right forepaw toward its raised forelegs, its very soft, lifted head immediately droops weakly to one side; its expression then is wonderfully amusing, a look of complete bewilderment.
units.source_zh: 我用我的右前脚朝着它那举起的两只前脚一拂，它那高高抬起的、非常柔软的头立刻毫无力气地向旁一歪，这时的表情可好玩啦，是一种发愣的样子。

paragraphs.source_zh: 如尊驾所知，我们猫儿不幸的是拿不了道具的，所以对于垒球棒啦、球啦，都不知道如何使用，加上即使会用，我们也没有钱去买。由于这两个原因，所以我选择的运动，必须是属于那种既不需要花费，也与运动器械无关的。既然是这样，也许有人会认为我可以慢条斯理地走走路或者叼着一片金枪鱼飞跑。但是只让我的四条腿做力学运动，利用地球引力的作用在大地上闯来闯去，未免过于简单乏味。尽管名称叫运动，但它像主人经常做的那样，只是在字面上运动来运动去，我认为这是玷污运动的神圣意义。当然，就是一般的运动，如果在某种刺激之下，也不一定不可以做。像“抢金枪鱼赛跑”、“寻找大马哈鱼”这类玩意儿，也是蛮有意思的。不过，这种场合缺不了对象，如果去掉对象的刺激，就变得索然寡味了。假如排除这些奖赏性的刺激物，那么我倒是想搞点带技巧性的运动。于是，我想出了各种方法。像从厨房的遮阳板跳到屋顶上去的运动，在屋脊的梅花形屋瓦上用四条腿站立的技巧，从晾衣竿上跑过去——这毕竟是难以指望成功的，因为竹竿滑溜溜的无法下爪子。还有从背后突然蹦到小孩身上——这虽是饶有兴味的运动，但经常搞就会大触霉头，所以至多每个月搞上三次。往头上套纸袋——这只能感到痛苦，是种兴趣不大的玩法，而且这种运动假如没有人和我合作，也无法进行，所以也不行。还有用我的爪子扒搔书的封皮，——这个运动一旦被主人发觉，不仅大有挨揍的可能，而且只锻炼了爪子的灵巧，不能锻炼浑身的肌肉。以上这些，都是旧式运动的内容。在新式运动中，有些是非常有趣的，首先是捕螳螂。捕螳螂虽不是捕老鼠那样的大运动，但它也不会有很大的危险。从仲夏到初秋这段期间，这种游戏是最属上乘的。至于说到捕捉的方法，我先到院中去寻出一只螳螂来，如果气候好，找出一两只是毫不费力的。然后，我就一阵风似的跑到螳螂身旁。这时螳螂一见来敌，立刻摆好架势，高高举起它那两个镰刀状的前脚。螳螂也是胆量很大的家伙，在没有领教对手的力量之前，总想较量一番，真是有意思极啦。我用我的右前脚朝着它那举起的两只前脚一拂，它那高高抬起的、非常柔软的头立刻毫无力气地向旁一歪，这时的表情可好玩啦，是一种发愣的样子。
